conditions.description: Front main cap and planets removed; keyed sun withdraws along open frontshaft.

Whole operating revolution, 128 intervals, all 14 driven gears and complete fixed structure. Exact current center orbits and fixed-sun gear ratios; initial loaded phases are in the assembly. Bulk clearance only: changed meshes require current fine tooth-contact evidence. Seat contact supplies necessary drive reachability, not sufficient tooth-transmission proof.

Service fixture: one production planet cap withdraws5.2mm with matching2.4mm-pitch rotation. This checks the common cap/post profile; other copies require correct initial helix phases. Rotating cap does not establish friction, tightening torque or resistance to loosening.
Front sun cap service withdrawal8.4mm at3.6mm pitch after bezel removal. Actual fitted initial cap phase must match the axle front thread.

Bezel caps removed; translate forward off its two posts.
Two removable small caps obstruct forward extraction.
Each bezel cap geometrically engages its own post thread; physical thread security unverified.
Two off-axis post/hole interfaces obstruct bezel rotation relative to carrier after their specified clearance; tests torque geometry only.
Front main cap obstructs sun extraction.
Fixed sun D key must resist rotation relative to hollow axle.
Direct axial extraction intersects axle thread; does not prove against unscrewing.
After bezel, planets, sun and frontcap removed, carrier slides off open shaft.
Carrier journal hub meets fixed sun after axial clearance.
Rearward carrier motion meets orangeannulus; this condition is a specific rear stop, not a clamping claim.
Carrier, sun and frontcap removed; orange D opening slides alongshaft.
Fixed axle shoulder obstructs rearward orange motion.
After rear support cap and wheel/core components removed, withdraw axle together with its front support lock towardfront. This avoids falsely pulling that cap through the collar.
Axle forward escape is obstructed by rear support cap through thread geometry; graph closes cap to collar.
Axle rearward escape is obstructed by front support cap through thread geometry.
Rear support cap meets collar rear face when pulled towardfront.
Front support cap meets collar front face when pulled rearward.
Axle D flat reacts sun torque into support collar.
Axle assembly removed; lift collar off open rectangular stem tongue.
Gravity-direction seating only; lifting the whole sculpture by wheel is expressly prohibited.
Collar removed; lift keyed stem from base and foot trim.
Stem lower end is supported by closed lid; this does not establish upward capture.
From closed 30-degree pose, tabs must obstruct downward escape. An optional separate service assembly provides the complete unlock-then-withdraw path.
Loose brass inlay seats intoVgroove; no positive upward retention claim.
Foot trim rests on base; no positive upward retention claim.

Lid rotates from closed30degree assemblypose back30degrees to entryslots. Withdrawal then belongs to an explicit service-state assembly with upper unit already removed; never pretend this check changes later condition startingposes.

Ballast service after upper assembly is removed or externally supported: lid rotates30degrees to slots, then withdraws12mm down. Pedestal is held clear of the table. This tests rigid path, not support forces.
